title: New Hire Success Pathway and Interview Evidence Rubric
summary: Combined hiring-to-onboard pathway: interview evidence rubric + 30/60/90 mentor checklist + buddy program notes. Designed to reduce time-to-productivity and improve calibration across hiring panels.
body:
PURPOSE:
Short doc to align people-ops, hiring managers, and interviewers on what counts as acceptable evidence in interviews and what mentors/buddies should do during the first 90 days.

SCOPE:
Applies to IC hiring (E, SRE, Product, Design) and early-career rotations. Separate senior leadership onboarding playbook elsewhere.

GOALS:
- Reduce variance in candidate pass/fail by 35% via clearer evidence expectations
- Ensure every new hire has a named mentor and documented 30/60/90 goals
- Cut first-billable-week by 20% for hire cohorts by enforcing checklist

HIGH-LEVEL FLOW (notes):
- Recruiter screens -> hiring manager + panel shortlist -> structured interview rounds (tech / systems / behavioral) -> rubric scoring -> offer & 1:1 manager onboarding plan -> assign mentor & buddy -> 30/60/90 execution + syncs

INTERVIEW EVIDENCE RUBRIC (for interviewers):
Guiding principle: capture "what candidate did" not just impressions. Use STAR-like fragments, attach concrete artifacts (code snippet, docs, diagrams).

Score legend: 1 = insufficient evidence, 2 = borderline, 3 = meets bar, 4 = strong, 5 = exceptional (rare)

Core dimensions (apply to all roles):
- Problem Framing (clarity of assumptions, scope, goal alignment) — examples: articulated constraints, trade-offs, asked clarifying Qs
- Depth of Reasoning (correctness, trade-off discussion, alternatives) — examples: explained failure modes, edge cases
- Execution Evidence (past work, repo links, design artifacts, performance numbers) — examples: PRs, metrics impact, before/after
- Collaboration & Communication (behavioral examples, conflict handling) — examples: peer feedback, cross-team work
- Role-specific skills (see below)

Technical role addendum (SWE/Infra/SRE):
- Systems thinking: candidate draws architecture, explains latencies, single point of failure, capacity planning
- Debugging: walking through root cause with logs/metrics, articulating reproducible steps
- Code quality: incremental improvements, testing strategy, telemetry
Evidence examples: small repo diff, short pseudo-code, postmortem excerpt

Product/Design role addendum:
- User-centered decisions: prioritized trade-offs tied to user impact
- Metrics literacy: select and defend metrics, define success criteria
- Design critique: provide before/after examples, accessible reasoning

INTERVIEWER NOTE TEMPLATE (copy into HireFlow comments):
- Q asked: [brief]
- Candidate response (evidence): [quote / paraphrase]
- Score per dimension: [numbers]
- Recommend: {hire | no-hire | follow-up}
- Artifacts linked: [URLs]

COMMON BIAS CHECKS (short):
- Was the same rubric applied to this candidate as others?
- Did we conflate culture fit with cultural match? Give concrete examples.
- Avoid relying solely on educational pedigree or previous employer brand

CALIBRATION PRACTICES (people-ops / hiring managers):
- Monthly calibration mini-sessions: 1h, review 3 recent decisions, invite 2 external panelists
- Quarterly rubric refresh: collect edge-case feedback, update wording

MENTOR & BUDDY PROGRAM (operational notes):
Definitions: Mentor = career + role development, longer-term (6 months). Buddy = day-to-day logistics, first 2 months.
Assignment: manager proposes mentor at offer stage; people-ops assigns buddy from same team within 72 hours of start.

30/60/90 CHECKLIST (for mentor & manager use) — copyable to new hire's onboarding doc:
Day 0–7 (onboarding week):
- [ ] Manager 30-min kickoff: expectations + immediate priorities
- [ ] Admin done: laptop, accounts, slack, jira, okta, calendar
- [ ] Buddy walk-through: team norms, rituals, pairing schedule
- [ ] First micro-task assigned (deliverable <= 3 days)

Days 8–30 (ramp):
- [ ] Weekly 1:1 with manager (focus: blockers, signals)
- [ ] Mentor 1:1 at least every 2 weeks
- [ ] Deliver first small project: code review / doc / design prototype
- [ ] Access to core dashboards + test env
- [ ] Peer-ship: 2 pairing sessions with cross-functional partners

Days 31–60 (consolidate):
- [ ] Lead small feature iteration or run a reliability test
- [ ] Present learnings to the team (15m demo)
- [ ] Performance metrics baseline established (latency / error / usage)
- [ ] Feedback loop: 360 check-in with mentor, buddy, manager

Days 61–90 (autonomy):
- [ ] Run a full lifecycle task from spec to rollout (can be limited scope)
- [ ] Own a recurring pager responsibility or monitoring dashboard
- [ ] Performance review touchpoint: "on-track / needs-support / exceptional"
- [ ] Mentor creates development plan for next 6 months

MENTOR CHECKLIST (practical tips):
- First week: send welcome note, schedule 30/60/90 syncs, share top 3 reading links
- Early days: do at least 2 pairing sessions; show how to use infra tools (deploys, dashboards)
- Month 1: provide 1 piece of specific, actionable feedback (not global praise)
- Ongoing: introduce the hire to 3 cross-team stakeholders

ONBOARDING ARTIFACTS (should exist in hire folder):
- Manager plan (PDF/Doc)
- Mentor notes (doc)
- First 90-day goals (copy of the checklist)
- Access logs + hardware receipt form
- First 30-day demo recording (if applicable)

EXAMPLE INTERVIEW SCENARIO (for panel runbook):
- 40 min: system design (whiteboard or Miro) + 20 min: behavioral deep-dive + 20 min: role-specific quick task. Interviewers should produce a single combined recommendation within 48h.

EVIDENCE STORAGE (practical):
- All interviewer notes to be pasted into HireFlow comments and linked artifacts attached. People-ops will snapshot these to the hire folder when offer is accepted.

LIGHTWEIGHT HIRING PLAN TEMPLATE (for managers):
- Role summary (2 lines)
- Success metrics first 6 months (3 metrics)
- Must-have skills (3) / Nice-to-have (2)
- Interview panel (names/roles)
- Target timeline (sourcing -> offer): 30 days ideal

RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS (todo):
- How to enforce mentor quality? (proposal: mentor scorecard, reward credit in performance review)
- Should we require a review of interview artifacts by people-ops for every hire under L4?
- How to track first-billable-week metric accurately across teams?

NEXT STEPS / OWNERSHIP:
- Evan to draft mentor scorecard template (due: 2026-02-10)
- Priya to add hire folder checklist to our drive automation (work with infra)
- Aisha to schedule first calibration session and invite panelists (by 2026-02-05)

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- keep rubric short — long rubrics get ignored.
- need a quick training slide deck for interviewers (10 slides max).
- consider pairing mentor allocation with hiring bonus for internal mentors.

SNIPPET: Example "behavioral evidence" entry to copy/paste into interview notes:
"Situation: Service X was repeatedly overloaded.
Task: reduce p95 latency by 30% on peak.
Action: introduced streaming cache + circuit-breaker; added production tracing and synthetic load tests.
Result: p95 dropped 35% under load tests; CC monitors removed several false alarms.
Artifacts: link to postmortem, PR #422."

END OF DOC — feedback welcomed, will iterate after first calibration session.
